text:
nora: Hi everyone, day 1 and I'm stuck. Cloned the dotfiles repo and ran the bootstrap script but asdf isn't picking up node/python versions. Also the script tries to pull a .local.env from the repo but it's missing (expected). Anyone have a short checklist for first-run setup? :wave:

sam: Welcome! Quick checklist I give new hires: 1) install Homebrew, 2) run `brew bundle --file Brewfile.local` from dotfiles if present, 3) ensure `eval "$(asdf init -)"` is in your shell rc before any PATH edits, 4) create a `~/.local.env` (gitignored) with tokens and secrets, 5) install direnv and allow it.

nora: thanks. The bootstrap script ran but when I open a new shell `node -v` says system node not asdf-managed.

sam: That usually means your shell didn't source asdf shims. Check `echo $PATH` and confirm `~/.asdf/shims` appears before `/usr/bin`. If not, move `eval "$(asdf init -)"` near top of `~/.zshrc` or `~/.bash_profile`. Also remember some terminals start non-login shells; put the init in both `~/.profile` and `~/.zshrc` to be safe.

devops: If you're on mac and used Homebrew, brew may have installed node at /usr/local/bin. You can remove conflicting brew symlinks with `brew unlink node` so asdf shims take precedence, or adjust PATH to put asdf earlier.

nora: got it. What's our recommended pattern for storing NPM / PyPI tokens securely?

sam: We use 1Password for secrets. Preferred flow: 1) install 1Password CLI `op`, 2) sign in and export tokens at session start but don't write them to dotfiles. Example in `~/.local.env` (gitignored): `NPM_TOKEN=... PYPI_TOKEN=...`. In CI we read tokens from vault. For local dev, you can create the file via `op item get "redwood-dev-tokens" --fields NPM_TOKEN, PYPI_TOKEN > ~/.local.env` but only if your 1Password policy allows scripting.

nora: direnv is in the dotfiles bootstrap. Anything extra to avoid accidental commits of local.env?

sam: Dotfiles repo includes a pre-commit hook that prevents `git add` of `~/.local.env` files by pattern, but double-check: `git status --ignored` to ensure it's ignored. Also run `git config --local core.hooksPath .githooks` after cloning to enable hooks.

devops: One more tip: VS Code's integrated shell sometimes launches without reading login rc. If you see different behavior between Terminal.app and VS Code terminal, try launching VS Code from the terminal (`code .`) so it inherits environment, or add `source ~/.profile` in your `~/.zprofile` so GUI shells get envs.

nora: The bootstrap did `asdf plugin-add python` but `asdf list python` is empty. How do I install the pinned versions?

sam: Run `asdf install` in the repo root if there's a `.tool-versions` file. That will install the pinned versions for all tools. If installs fail, paste the error — common causes: missing build deps (on mac run `brew install openssl readline libffi`), or proxy/CA issues which cause downloads to fail.

nora: I'm behind a corporate proxy and saw curl SSL errors when asdf tried to fetch tarballs. Any minimal steps?

devops: Add corp CA to system trust store (mac: `sudo security add-trusted-cert -d -r trustRoot -k /Library/Keychains/System.keychain /path/to/corp.crt`). If proxy requires auth, run a local proxy (cntlm) and export `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` in `~/.local.env`. Make sure both uppercase and lowercase envs are set because some tools use lowercase.

nora: perfect — I'll try these. One last question: how do I contribute small tweaks to dotfiles without exposing secrets?

sam: Branch from your fork, keep secrets in `~/.local.env` only, and add a README snippet explaining how to rehydrate secrets with 1Password commands. If you need to test a change that requires tokens, use a local feature branch and never push the file. We usually review dotfile PRs for safety.

hr-bot: Welcome nora! Completed onboarding checklist items: "dotfiles repo cloned", "Brew installed". Remaining suggested items: "Add corp CA if needed", "Install 1Password CLI", "Run asdf install from repo root". https://internal.redwood/onboarding/checklist

nora: Awesome, thanks all — will report back once the CA + asdf install completes. :raised_hands:
